assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT turned the strongly correlated electron problem into a tractable, systematically improvable framework (exact in infinite dimensions, mapped onto a quantum impurity problem). Combined with DFT (LDA+DMFT) it is now a working tool for real correlated materials, Mott transitions, heavy fermions and transition-metal oxides. As someone who works daily with electronic-structure methods and their limits for correlated systems, I regard this as the most consequential theory-to-materials advance on the list.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit and the Georges-Kotliar mapping to an Anderson impurity model are the decisive steps; all three credited names are well supported. Others (e.g. Müller-Hartmann, Jarrell, Rozenberg, Krauth) contributed but are not in the credited set, so the trio is a defensible but not perfectly complete configuration.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent use and validation, broad adoption across community codes, and extensions (cluster DMFT, LDA+DMFT) make this mature. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Exact credit division between the 1989 infinite-dimension work and the 1992 impurity mapping is somewhat contested; the trio omits other contributors.
Quantitative accuracy for low-dimensional and strongly nonlocal correlations is limited, which a citation must frame carefully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with the HgTe experimental realization, opened a field linking band topology, spin-orbit coupling and surface states, and reshaped materials searches. It is clear, original and has lasting impact, with direct relevance to spin-orbit-driven magnetism and electronic-structure classification of materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supply the theory (Z2 invariant, graphene QSH); Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental QSH in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, and the 3D-TI experimentalists (Hasan, Cava, Shen) are not in the credited names, so the allocation is incomplete and contested.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many independent groups with ARPES, transport and theory; the concept is stable and has become textbook. Timely, with growing pressure given the age of key theorists.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit relative to Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes, Hasan, Fu, and others not on the credited list.
Practical device impact remains modest compared with the conceptual impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire quantum materials field. The system is a tunable platform for correlated physics, which as a first-principles theorist I find compelling since continuum models and ab initio approaches both matter here.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer-MacDonald's continuum model predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery in 2018. Cao and Kim/Efetov-type contributions and earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) are not credited, so allocation is partial.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly replicated and extended across many groups, but the field is under a decade old; mechanism of superconductivity and nature of correlated states remain debated. Somewhat early but strong.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and sample-dependent reproducibility remain unsettled.
Earlier theoretical precursors and the lead student's role complicate credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance, and especially coherent spin-dependent tunnelling in Fe/MgO/Fe, underpins hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It is a magnetism-and-spintronics advance combining solid-state physics and first-principles prediction, with huge technological reach.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki (and Moodera) demonstrated room-temperature TMR in 1995; Butler/Mathon predicted giant TMR in epitaxial MgO; Parkin and Yuasa realized it experimentally in 2004. Butler is credited but I give priority to the experimental trio; the choice excludes a theory contribution that I, as a theorist, find important, and Moodera is absent from the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: two decades of industrial deployment, confirmed repeatedly. Recognition is timely, though the spintronics field already received the 2007 GMR prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may weigh against it.
Fair division between the early amorphous-barrier discovery and the MgO coherent-tunnelling breakthrough is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of skyrmion lattices in chiral magnets (MnSi) and real-space imaging, then at room temperature, established topological spin textures with emergent electrodynamics. This is squarely in the realm of magnetism and spin dynamics where I work; the discovery is conceptually clear and linked to Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya physics.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's neutron work on MnSi, Tokura's real-space Lorentz TEM observation, and Wiesendanger's atomic-scale skyrmion lattice in Fe/Ir(111) are key; theory by Bogdanov and Rossler et al. is not in the credited set, which is a notable gap.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many material classes and by multiple techniques, but technological promise (racetrack memory) remains unproven; the field is maturing but not yet stable in application terms.
uncertainties: Theoretical originators (Bogdanov, Rossler) are not credited.
Device relevance remains speculative, which may make recognition premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spin Hall and inverse spin Hall effects enable generation and detection of spin currents electrically, and are central to spin-orbit torque switching, ultrafast spin dynamics and spintronics. The physics (spin-orbit coupling, Berry-curvature contributions) is important and I know the first-principles side well.
assessment.attribution: Dyakonov and Perel predicted the effect in 1971; Saitoh demonstrated electrical detection via inverse spin Hall; Jungwirth contributed experimental and theoretical work on the intrinsic and anomalous Hall variants. Awschalom's optical observation is also decisive but I limit to three. The spread of contributions makes a clean trio difficult.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and widely used; some foundational interpretations (intrinsic vs extrinsic mechanisms) are settled, but credit is diffuse.
uncertainties: Attribution is diffuse, with Hirsch, Zhang, Kato, Wunderlich, Sinova and others contributing.
Time gap and credit split may make a clean citation hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate and foundational schemes for quantum simulation with cold atoms, shaping quantum information experiments. The ideas are original and have lasting influence, though from my perspective further from materials physics.
assessment.attribution: The two credited names cover the proposals cleanly and constitute a natural pairing. Experimental realization belongs to other candidates (Blatt, Wineland) so this recognition is theory-only.
assessment.maturity: Proposals decades old, extensively realized in trapped ions and atom arrays; recognition is well timed, though the broader quantum-computing prize landscape is crowded.
uncertainties: Overlap with other quantum-information candidates may dilute the case.
Wineland's 2012 prize already recognized related experimental work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with magic-wavelength trapping reached 10^-18 precision and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. A clear, important measurement advance, though outside my core field, so I weigh it with some caution.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and Ye demonstrated record performance; the two names are a clean pair, though Hall and Hänsch (2005) and other clock groups also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed, with several independent labs reaching comparable accuracy; SI redefinition of the second remains pending, so full impact is still unfolding.
uncertainties: Redefinition of the second has not occurred, so impact may be premature.
Relation to the 2005 frequency comb prize and single-ion clocks (Wineland) could complicate novelty.
